title: Local rational lifting of generic semiabelian Picard classes modulo algebraic equivalence
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$. The addition, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume every geometric fibre is semiabelian: after an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$, it fits into an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,k}^r\to G_k\to A_k\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, and $A_k$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme. Write $\eta$ for the generic point and $K=\kappa(\eta)$. For a $K$-scheme $X$, write $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], with tensor product as addition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\mathrm{geom}}(X)$ for the subgroup of geometrically algebraically trivial classes. For a finite-type scheme $X$ over a field, geometric algebraic equivalence means the equivalence relation, after extension to an algebraic closure of the ground field, generated by two fibres of an invertible module on $X\times T$, where $T$ is a smooth connected variety over that algebraic closure. A line is geometrically algebraically trivial when it is equivalent to $\mathcal O_X$ in this sense. For every $s\in S$ and every $\alpha\in\operatorname{Pic}(G_\eta)/\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\mathrm{geom}}(G_\eta)$ there are an affine open neighbourhood $W\subseteq S$ of $s$, an integer $n\geq1$ and an invertible module $M$ on $G_W=G\times_SW$ such that the class of $M_\eta$ in this quotient is $n\alpha$. Equivalently, the union, over affine neighbourhoods $W$ of $s$, of the images of $\operatorname{Pic}(G_W)$ in that quotient has torsion cokernel. Restriction is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. No positivity or symmetry hypothesis is imposed, and no isomorphism $M_\eta\simeq L^{\otimes n}$ is asserted for a representative $L$ of $\alpha$.

source.place: XI Theorem 1.13, Picard-class extension input, separated from positivity; compare Moret-Bailly II 3.3.3. Original local WANTED. This quotient formulation is agent-written, not a verbatim transcription or a claimed reading of the missing theorem.

proof.text: Choose an invertible module $L$ representing $\alpha$. Its identity fibre is a one-dimensional $K$-vector space, so choose a basis and rigidify it. Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-second-difference-diagonal] to $H=G_\eta$. The given geometric-fibre hypothesis includes this generic fibre; smoothness restricts by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], and finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). A finitely presented morphism is of finite type by its affine finite-generator definition. We obtain a biextension $D=D_2(L)$ on $G_\eta\times_KG_\eta$ whose diagonal pullback has quotient class $2\alpha$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-semiabelian-biextension-extension] to the pair $(P,Q)=(G,G)$ over the given $S$. Its normality, integrality, local Noetherianity, smoothness, separatedness, finite presentation and semiabelian geometric-fibre hypotheses are exactly those of the item. There is an invertible module $E$ on $G\times_SG$, with biextension laws and a biextension isomorphism $E_\eta\simeq D$.

source.place: II Theorem 3.6, generic-fibre equivalence for biextensions, connected-fibre case. Primary theorem statement located online in Numdam search; local original WANTED.

external.place: Revised 2021 thesis Theorem 3.3.2.6 (printed p.70, PDF p.84), read online at https://www.kwlan.org/articles/cpt-PEL-type-thesis-revision-dense.pdf

proof.text: Let $\Delta:G\to G\times_SG$ be the diagonal and put $N=\Delta^*E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1),(2), $N$ is invertible and $N_\eta\simeq\Delta_\eta^*D$: both pullback composites are the same map into $G\times_SG$, so functoriality identifies them. Thus step 1 gives $[N_\eta]=2\alpha$. For each $s$ choose an affine open neighbourhood $W$ and set $M=N|_{G_W}$, $n=2$. Its generic restriction is still $N_\eta$. This proves the requested assertion. The union of images is a subgroup: restrict any two lines to a common affine neighbourhood of $s$ and tensor them, or take the dual for the negative. Such a common affine neighbourhood exists inside the intersection of their opens. Every element of the quotient by this subgroup is killed by $2$, hence its cokernel is torsion. Conversely, being torsion says exactly that every class has a positive multiple in the union.
